purpose: Authentic evidence excerpts for the authorized ITT revision. These are historical reports and official documentary editions, not invented newspaper layouts or recreations of internal memoranda.
coordinatePolicy: Crop and highlight coordinates remain null until computed from the actual PDF page by the cloud media preparer. Text anchors and one-based PDF page numbers were checked against the original text; no normalized boxes have been guessed.

documents.caption: U.S. Senate report · 1973 · Negotiations in 1971
documents.evidenceSummary: The Senate describes ITT demanding $153 million for its telephone interest, Chile offering $24 million, and an impasse concerning management during proposed international arbitration.
documents.editorialLimit: These are negotiating positions. The passage does not establish a fair market valuation, realized loss, or completed international arbitration.
documents.credit: U.S. Senate, The International Telephone and Telegraph Company and Chile, 1970–71 (1973), p.14. U.S. Government publication; public domain.
documents.changes: Crop for legibility and restrained amber highlights; preserve source paragraph and page attribution. No text substitution.

documents.caption: U.S. Senate report · 1973 · Merriam's 1971 proposal
highlightTextAnchors: Peterson testified that he took no action
documents.evidenceSummary: After Geneen's lunch with Peterson and Haig, Geneen instructed Merriam to put ITT suggestions in writing. Merriam sent Peterson an October 1, 1971 letter with an eighteen-point action plan. Peterson testified that he did not implement it.
documents.editorialLimit: This is the Senate's later account, not the original 1971 letter. The report describes circulation and no evidenced disagreement from Geneen or Gerrity; that does not prove formal endorsement of every item by the full board. A proposal and its execution remain separate.
documents.credit: U.S. Senate, The International Telephone and Telegraph Company and Chile, 1970–71 (1973), p.15. U.S. Government publication; public domain.
documents.changes: Crop around the report's account of the letter and nonimplementation. Do not label this excerpt as the original letter.

documents.caption: U.S. Senate report · 1973 · Executives' account of the talks
documents.evidenceSummary: The report summarizes executive testimony that negotiations over international appraisal continued until Anderson's disclosures, after which a planned Guilfoyle–Letelier meeting was canceled and negotiations were broken off.
documents.editorialLimit: Attribute the explanation of the rupture to Guilfoyle/Geneen testimony. The paragraph continues from printed p.15; a crop must preserve enough context and may be introduced as their account. Use March 1972 in narration because the report and FRUS differ by one day over the first column.
documents.credit: U.S. Senate, The International Telephone and Telegraph Company and Chile, 1970–71 (1973), pp.15–16. U.S. Government publication; public domain.
documents.changes: Top-of-page authentic report excerpt with amber emphasis. Not a facsimile of Anderson's newspaper column or the original negotiating memorandum.

documents.caption: Senator Church's hypothetical · Senate report, 1973
documents.evidenceSummary: Church inverts the case: a British corporation offers support for a British government plan to prevent the American candidate with most votes from becoming president through the U.S. Congress. McCone says he would be distressed by such foreign-government and corporate interference.
documents.editorialLimit: The British case is expressly hypothetical. The Senate report reproduces the exchange from McCone testimony; no invented reaction, private dialogue, or imitation archival voice may be added.
documents.credit: U.S. Senate, The International Telephone and Telegraph Company and Chile, 1970–71 (1973), p.17, quoting McCone testimony. U.S. Government publication; public domain.
documents.changes: Crop the genuine question/answer, retaining attribution and enough surrounding text to identify the hypothetical. Amber highlights follow the real printed words.

documents.caption: State Department memorandum · March 16, 1973
documents.evidenceSummary: The contemporary memorandum describes the $92.5 million ITT claim, management's proposed refusal on contractual grounds, and expected arguments if ITT resisted through arbitration.
documents.editorialLimit: Use the body paragraph, not editorial footnote 3, as the 1973 document. Expected arbitration is not evidence that arbitration later occurred. Footnote 3 supplies a later indemnification account citing Nathaniel Davis; the DFC ledger independently supplies the final amounts. The FRUS typography is an authentic official documentary edition, not the original classified page layout.
documents.credit: U.S. Department of State, Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume XXI (2014), document 322, p.850; memorandum of March 16, 1973. U.S. Government work; public domain.
documents.changes: Crop the actual FRUS PDF paragraph; retain period/document identification. Do not retype or fabricate classified memo styling.

documents.caption: Official OPIC claims ledger · Fiscal 1975 settlement
documents.evidenceSummary: The ITT/Chile/telephone/expropriation row continuing the FY1975 section records a $94,091,531 settlement, comprising $34,706,917 cash and $59,384,614 guaranty amount.
documents.editorialLimit: Preserve the cash and guaranty column headings. The FY1975 heading is on preceding PDF p.4, while the ITT row continues on p.5; caption provides that checked context. A guarantee is not cash paid that day. The total is not profit or evidence that all losses were recovered. Small exact-dollar differences exist against the FRUS editorial note; use this institutional ledger for the amounts.
documents.credit: Overseas Private Investment Corporation / U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, Claims and Arbitral Awards, FY1966–FY2019, PDF p.5, ITT/Chile row. U.S. Government publication; public domain.
documents.changes: Retain table title, amount-column headings and the complete ITT row. Crop unrelated lower-year rows for reading. Amber emphasis must distinguish cash from guarantees.

existingEvidenceToPreserve.caption: Senate investigation · At least $350,000 to the campaign
existingEvidenceToPreserve.editorialLimit: This is corporate funding reported to have reached a campaign, distinct from the proposed $1 million that CIA did not accept. The NARA file is an archival staff-report version; confirm its printed pagination visually rather than copying pagination from another edition.

existingEvidenceToPreserve.caption: Senate report · September 1970 congressional proposal
existingEvidenceToPreserve.editorialLimit: The September offer concerned the remaining congressional selection after the popular vote. Do not collapse it into the earlier candidate-funding approach or imply acceptance. This is the same source page as the negotiation-break excerpt; account for page identity when limiting image reuse.

factualCorrectionsSentToRoot.issue: The phrase 'while its value went to arbitration' could imply completed arbitration, while the cited Senate passage describes a proposal that met an impasse.
factualCorrectionsSentToRoot.suggestedReplacement: during a proposed arbitration over its value

factualCorrectionsSentToRoot.issue: Neither the FRUS322 body nor editorial note establishes an eventual completed arbitration. The body anticipates possible arbitration; the DFC ledger establishes a later settlement.
factualCorrectionsSentToRoot.suggestedReplacement: The record traces a proposed refusal and a later insurance settlement recorded in fiscal 1975.
